classification.difficultyReason: Combines direct volume calculation, inverse use of the volume formula with mixed units, and recovery of dimensions from three face areas.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with dimensions $5.2\text{ cm}\times6\text{ cm}\times10\text{ cm}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: A right rectangular prism has volume $625\text{ mm}^3$. The height of the prism is $12.5\text{ cm}$. Find the area of the base.

answer.worked:
Use consistent units: $12.5\text{ cm}=125\text{ mm}$. Since $V=Ah$,
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{V}{h}\\A&=\frac{625}{125}\\A&=5\text{ mm}^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: The three distinct face areas of a right rectangular prism are $35\text{ cm}^2$, $50\text{ cm}^2$ and $70\text{ cm}^2$. Find the volume of the prism.

answer.short:
$350\text{ cm}^3$.

The dimensions are $5\text{ cm}$, $7\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$.
answer.worked:
The dimensions must give the three face areas as pairwise products. Factor pairs give
$$\begin{align*}35&=5\times7\\50&=5\times10\\70&=7\times10\end{align*}$$
Thus the dimensions are $5\text{ cm}$, $7\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}V&=lwh\\V&=5\times7\times10\\V&=350\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$
